thread:
maria: heads-up — seeing a spike of fncall invalid-shape rejects from EU region. Dashboard shows ~1.2k in the last 6h, many flagged as routed->degen. who owns the classification labels/ux for this?
kevin: I can take classification rules, but we need design input on how to surface it. current dashboard has a single 'fncall rejects' bucket which is useless.
sophia: +1. From infra side, routing policy treats any schema-reject as failover to degen model and counts toward customer quota. we should decide whether schema-rejects should be billed.
lucas: billing product hates silent counts. if we bill, customers will complain if their model hallucinated tool outputs. maybe we should not bill for schema rejects routed to degen.
maria: we also need to tag telemetry so we can differentiate: reject_due_to_interface, reject_due_to_timeout, reject_due_to_parse_error. right now it's just "reject". can we plumb these tags end-to-end?
kevin: agree. propose events: `fncall.reject.reason:{interface|timeout|parse|enum-mismatch}` and `routing.decision:{fallback|retry|drop}`. Then dashboard filters can join those.
sophia: that sounds good. but change impacts metrics schema in observability; retention + cost. we'll need a migration plan and a sample rate. can we sample 1% full payloads and attach reason tags to aggregated counts?
lucas: For billing we need deterministic behavior. my suggestion: if routing.decision==fallback and reject.reason==interface, do not bill. otherwise bill. simple rule.
maria: what about UX? product wants a per-route toggle in console: `treat schema rejects as billable` with explanation. toggles default to off for new customers.
kevin: console change is straightforward, but need endpoint to surface counts per route with breakouts. SQL for metrics team: `SELECT sum(count) FROM metrics WHERE route=$ROUTE AND tag='fncall.reject.reason:interface'`.
sophia: note: some downstream adaptors can coerce shapes. can we add a small heuristic: if coercion succeeded, mark as `coerced` and treat as billing-ok? e.g., `reject.reason=coerce_success`
lucas: I worry about edge cases — coerced outputs might be wrong. billing policy should be conservative: only waive billing when we both coerced AND unit-tests (small schema checks) passed.
maria: ok action items: 1) kevin: PR for telemetry labels + schema (include sample keys). 2) sophia: change routing to emit routing.decision tag and coercion flag. 3) lucas: write billing decision matrix and sample customer-friendly console copy. 4) design: short UX mock for per-route toggle (cc @design).
kevin: I'll open a draft PR with examples. sample event payload in PR: ```{ "event":"fncall.reject","route":"/chat/generate","reason":"interface","routing":"fallback","coerced":false }```
maria: nice. can we also log a minimal example of the invalid payload to a secure PII-safe store for debugging (sampled)? sophia thoughts?
sophia: yes, we can send a sampled redact pipeline. we'll keep 1 in 1000 full payloads and shorten identifiers. deploy-bot: deployment scheduled: telemetry-proto v2 -> staging at 10:00 UTC today :rocket:
maria: perfect. let's review the PR tomorrow. :thumbsup:
